text:
maria: Heads-up — we need to finalize the handshake semantics between the canary traffic router and SRE probes before the next deploy window. Current gaps: probe backoff, partial-traffic kill switch, and what counts as a 'fallback-ready' model.

leo: Agree. My read: keep the decision logic in the control plane (rollout service) and keep router dumb (weights + version map). Router should expose simple signals only: health, p99, error-rate, and an allow-fallback flag.

sami: +1 for control plane. But must be careful around session affinity: if we switch variant mid-session we break KV cache affinity and can blow up latency. We need a session-drain period or sticky cookie with version namespace.

olivia: Thinking about fallback targets: cheap quantized variant, smaller model, region-fallback, or degrade to safety response. Which order? Also want explicit fallthrough policy so customer requests don't leak to private variants.

maria: Proposed order: 1) local model variant (quantized), 2) regional equivalent, 3) safety-mode (short hardcoded reply), 4) circuit reject. Keep rollout service configurable per-customer.

leo: For failure detection: use composite signal: (p99 > threshold) OR (errors rate > threshold) OR (model-level rejects > X). Use sliding windows and require sustained breach for 30s before action. Also add escalation if breach persists — increase fallback percentage.

sami: What about graceful degrade vs sharp cut? For A/B we can ramp weight down by 20% steps with 1m observation windows. For canary we should allow immediate 100% cut if safety trigger matches (exploit/PII leak).

olivia: Agreed. We should also version the heuristics as policy objects so product teams can tune per-customer SLOs. Example policy blob:```json
{
  "name": "canary-default",
  "p99_ms": 300,
  "error_rate_pct": 1.0,
  "sustained_secs": 30,
  "ramp_step_pct": 20,
  "fallback_targets": ["quantized-v2","regional-us-east-1","safety-mode"]
}
```

maria: Nice. Router API then needs a tiny endpoint: /decisions?route=foo returns {versionWeights, allowFallback, reasonCode}. Keep it idempotent and snapshot at config push.

eng-sre-bot: deployment-notice: canary-run started for model-redwood-7b at 2187654300 — monitoring alerts enabled. :rotating_light:

leo: Observability: emit events: fallback.triggered (with target, reason, percentage), canary.metrics.{latency,p99,err} and decision.evaluated. Keep a trace id tied to each decision for debugging.

sami: Also add a probe handshake: before routing >0% traffic to new model, run an isolated probe workload that simulates typical request shapes and warms KV cache. Probe must succeed for N consecutive runs (default 3) and be within p50/p99 bounds. If probe warms caches, mark warm=true and allow sticky sessions.

olivia: Edge-case: partial node failures inside pool — router should be able to mark specific instances unhealthy and shift weight inside same version. We need instance-level health checks feeding into the rollout service.

maria: Runbook notes for oncall: fallback auto triggers should post to #incidents with summary + one-click revert button (UI triggers rollback in control plane). If oncall clicks revert, rollout service should immediately pin previous version and drain requests for the failed variant.

leo: Security note: fallback telemetry must not include customer PII. Tag sampling at ingress.

maria: Next steps: I'll draft an RFC with the control-plane policy schema, router API spec, and probe contract. @olivia can you mock the policy UI knobs? @sami can you outline the session-affinity drain procedure? @leo please write the telemetry event contract. I'll include the runbook snippet.

olivia: On it, will post a quick mock by EOD. :+1:

sami: I'll sketch drain flow and TTL-based sticky keys.

leo: Telemetry contract draft incoming tomorrow AM.

maria: Great — thanks. If no objections I'll spin the RFC tomorrow.

eng-sre-bot: note: thread archived automatically after 7 days of inactivity.
